world: TEST (stand-in batch RPC store, real executor + production sources over a fake PostgREST; boards SYNTHETIC sandbox)

leg1_discovery.label: TEST
leg1_discovery.note: the worker's own postingsFor over the shared KB pool loader (600-row recency window); served = rows the window yielded, before screening

leg2_prepare.label: TEST (ends DOORSTEP by design)
leg2_prepare.residual_note: prepare drain wall − leg 1 − wrapped store/profile seams; includes 155 screen + tailor and the per-posting doorstep drives

leg3_approval.label: TEST (stand-in store, real RPC shape + real 155 hash re-verification)
leg3_approval.attribution: pending+claim+readRun seams in the approve drain + approveRun's card-hash re-verification and approval mint timed directly on a restored clone of the stored run (the recorded approval is the executor's own, in the same drain)

leg4_drain_batch.label: TEST + SYNTHETIC boards (policy outcome — caps enforced by real 149, unmodified)
leg4_drain_batch.execution_overhead_note: approve drain wall − board calls − store/profile seams − the approval mint: executeRun's in-process loop cost (per-posting session rebuild + runApply payload rebuild + cap check) across ALL selected postings, including the ones the caps then deferred
leg4_drain_batch.note: executeRun's loop is serial: one posting's drive completes before the next begins; drives re-run the doorstep drive before submitting (sessions do not survive between the prepare and approve invocations). Board-call time here is in-process (µs-scale against the sandbox board) — the per-drive cost that matters is measured whole in the CAPACITY drain.

not_run.leg: approval via the LIVE career_batch_* RPCs
not_run.label: NOT_RUN
not_run.missing: an operator env + a chat-committed intent for a real user — this harness never writes live intents; the approval leg runs at the identical wire shape against the stand-in store and is labeled TEST

not_run.leg: drain against LIVE boards via the worker host board service
not_run.label: NOT_RUN
not_run.missing: the board-service binding on the worker host (the throughput lane's live drives own that seam); this harness's drain is SYNTHETIC (sandbox boards) inside the submit gate, or DOORSTEP in --mode doorstep

not_run.label: NOT_RUN
not_run.missing: the closure schema (career_apply_* stack) is not live on the project yet; the batch approval measured here is the live 20261016010000 intent + card-hash path

capacity_drain.label: CAPACITY (per-drive marginals through the real 149 submit gate; boards SYNTHETIC)

projection.label: PROJECTION from measured marginals (TEST world, SYNTHETIC boards)
projection.basis_note: the per-drive marginal is IN-PROCESS cost (149 payload build, gates, sandbox board) — it excludes live-board latency (browser launch, page loads, network), which is the NOT_RUN live-board leg owned by the throughput lane. Read this projection as the pipeline's CPU-side ceiling, never as a live submission rate.
projection.note: capacity projection — what the pipeline can physically drive in 30 min; the policy outcome for one user's batch is leg 4's submitted (cap-bound) number, reported separately and never merged with this one

binding_constraint: product caps (by design, owner ruling): the batch drain stopped at 5 submitted with 45 deferred CAP_REACHED — caps are the binding constraint on single-user submissions in any world; throughput is not
